title: Push, approve, execute: the intent travels intact
takeaway: The intent is pushed once, held by the server, shown to the user, copied into the token, and checked again when the token is used.

steps.say: {{agent}} pushes the request to the authorization server. The intent ({{item}}, {{currency}} {{amount}}) travels in the back channel, so the browser never carries it.
The browser opens /authorize with only client_id and request_uri. The server resolves the stored request and burns the request_uri.
{{user}} sees the exact intent and approves it. The approval names the hash of what was shown.
{{agent}} redeems the code. The access token carries the bound intent as authorization_details and an intent claim.
{{agent}} uses the token for the approved action. The resource server finds the request equal to the bound intent and runs it.

title: The agent proposes, the human approves the exact intent
takeaway: The approval is for one specific action. The same token cannot be reused for a dearer one, a different target, or a second run.

steps.say: {{agent}} proposes the action on {{user}}'s behalf: {{item}}, {{currency}} {{amount}}. Nothing has been approved yet.
{{user}}'s browser is sent to the authorization server with request_uri only.
{{user}} reads the intent and approves exactly that: {{item}} for {{currency}} {{amount}}.
The token is minted with that intent in it.
The approved action runs once.
The agent tries the same token for {{currency}} {{amount_tampered}}. Refused: {{user}} approved {{currency}} {{amount}}, not this.
The agent replays the exact approved action. Refused: the intent was used once and that was the approval.

title: Amount edited in the browser link
takeaway: With PAR, parameters beside request_uri are refused, so editing the link cannot change what was pushed.

steps.say: {{agent}} pushes a request for {{currency}} {{amount}}.
Someone edits the authorize link to add an intent for {{currency}} {{amount_tampered}}. The server honours only client_id and request_uri and refuses the rest.

title: Approval submitted for a different intent
takeaway: Consent is bound to the intent hash. An approval that names a different intent is refused, so a swapped consent screen cannot launder an approval.

steps.say: {{agent}} pushes the request for {{currency}} {{amount}}.
The server resolves it and opens a consent transaction.
The approval that comes back names the hash of a {{currency}} {{amount_tampered}} intent, not the one bound at PAR. Refused.

title: Resource swapped at the token request
takeaway: A token request may not change the bound intent. The server compares it with what was pushed and approved.

steps.say: {{agent}} pushes the request for the approved target.
{{user}} approves.
At the token endpoint the client asks for a different resource. The server sees a different intent than the one approved and refuses.

title: Valid token, different target
takeaway: A genuine token is still only good for its own intent. The resource server compares what is attempted with the bound intent.

steps.say: A real token is issued for the approved intent.
The agent aims the token at {{resource_swapped}}. The resource server refuses: the bound resource is different.

title: Valid token, bigger amount
takeaway: The approved amount is a ceiling that is also a floor: the action must equal the intent, not merely stay under a scope.

steps.say: The agent asks to move {{currency}} {{amount_tampered}} with a token approved for {{currency}} {{amount}}. Refused.
A different action ({{action_other}}) with the same token. Also refused.

title: request_uri replayed
takeaway: A request_uri is one-time. Whoever sees it in a log or history cannot use it again.

steps.say: {{agent}} pushes the request.
First use: resolved and burned.
A second open of the same request_uri is refused.

title: request_uri used after it expired
takeaway: A pushed request lives for 60 seconds. A stale link is useless.

steps.say: {{agent}} pushes the request. expires_in is 60.
The mock clock moves forward 61 seconds. Nobody opened the link.
The authorization server refuses the expired request_uri.

title: request_uri presented by another client
takeaway: A request_uri belongs to the client that pushed it.

steps.say: {{agent}} (agent-app) pushes the request.
A different client, partner-app, presents that request_uri. Refused, and the request_uri is not burned.

title: Pushed request with no intent
takeaway: This server will not issue authorization without knowing what it is for.

steps.say: {{agent}} pushes a request with no intent. A bare scope would be a blank cheque, so the server refuses.

title: Inline parameters when PAR is required
takeaway: When a client is set to require PAR, an authorize request with inline parameters is refused outright. That is what makes PAR enforceable.

steps.say: The client skips PAR and sends the intent as plain query parameters. The server was told this client must push, so it refuses.

title: Contrast: no PAR, the link can be edited
takeaway: Without PAR the intent rides in the browser, where it can be changed. The server binds whatever arrives, so the token faithfully carries the edited intent.

steps.say: A legacy client is not required to use PAR. A link was edited in transit to ask for {{currency}} {{amount_tampered}} instead of {{currency}} {{amount}}.
The consent screen shows what arrived. If {{user}} does not read it, it is approved.
The tampered action runs. PAR would have prevented this: the browser would not have carried the amount at all.

title: Token edited to raise the amount
takeaway: The intent claim is signed. Editing it breaks the signature.

steps.say: A genuine token is issued for the approved intent.
The payload is edited to {{currency}} {{amount_tampered}} and the old signature kept. The resource server verifies the signature and refuses it.

title: Unregistered parameter in the push
takeaway: This server is strict: parameters it does not know are refused rather than silently ignored.

steps.say: {{agent}} sneaks an extra parameter into the push. It is not part of the registered set, so the server refuses the whole request.
